subject: Pilot Enablement: Decision Path, Security Gate, and Champion Brief
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pilot Enablement: Decision Path, Security Gate, and Champion Brief

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from the discovery and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on decision makers, procurement gates, and how we support your internal champion (looks like Elena will own that).

What we heard
- Primary use case: customer support triage + contextual responses for high-value accounts (reducing mean time to resolution on P1s).
- Success criteria: 40% reduction in time-to-first-response and 10% deflection of tier-1 tickets in the pilot window.
- Data scope: subset of support transcripts + knowledge base articles; no PHI expected.

Stakeholders noted
- Economic / budget owner: Marco Bianchi (Head of Ops) — final sign-off on pilot budget.
- Security / infosec reviewer: external vendor security team + their internal InfoSec (requested SOC 2 + data flow diagram).
- Procurement: standard SOW + PO process; likely procurement lead assigned after legal redlines.
- Champion: Elena (will coordinate internal demos and act as day-to-day advocate).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) I’ll send a short pilot pack (ROI one-pager, security FAQ answers, and an MAP template) you can share with Marco and the procurement team.
2) Please confirm who on your side owns procurement and InfoSec intake (name + email).
3) Recommended next meeting: a 30-minute procurement/security sync next week to review answers and identify gating items.

Attached: RIF-pilot-ROI-one-pager.pdf (one-slide ROI), Security-FAQ-answers.docx, Mutual-Action-Plan-template.xlsx.

If this matches your notes, happy to get the procurement sync on the calendar — propose Thu 9/18 10am PT or Fri 9/19 11am PT.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Thanks for the concise recap — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Marco is the economic approver but procurement will own the PO. Procurement lead is Bianca Liu (bianca.liu@nebulafinance.com) — I’ll loop her in once we have answers to InfoSec questions.
- InfoSec: we run a vendor intake that looks for SOC 2 Type II + data retention and deletion policies. I did want to flag that we will likely ask for an on-premise option evaluation if there are any red flags.
- Timeline: our Q4 procurement calendar is tight; a pilot needs to be kicked off by mid-Oct to qualify for our year-end budget.

Can you give a short bulleted ROI line I can paste into the internal note for Marco (one sentence + expected cost delta)? Also please call out any absolute blockers we should expect from a security perspective.

Aditya / Tessa —

Drafts below; I kept the ROI conservative and the security memo short so Elena can forward without edits. I also included a 2-line talk track Elena can use with Marco to frame the ask to the economic owner.

1) One-line ROI for Marco (paste-ready):
"Expected pilot outcome: ~40% faster time-to-first-response on prioritized queues, translating to an estimated 18–22% reduction in human-handled hours for the pilot cohort and a projected monthly operational savings of $9k–$12k at full production scale."

2) Security blockers / short memo (paste-ready):
"Summary: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we will provide a security FAQ and data flow diagram. For the pilot, data scope is limited to redacted support transcripts and knowledge-base content; no PHI or payment data will be ingested. On-premise hosting is available as an option but adds an estimated 6–8 week lead time and a modest platform premium — we recommend a hosted pilot while we validate controls, then evaluate private deployment if InfoSec requires it."

3) Champion talk track (2 lines Elena can use in a quick slack/email to Marco):
"This pilot reduces time-to-first-response by ~40% for high-priority accounts with minimal engineering effort. It’s a low-risk, budgeted 8-week test to validate efficiency gains before a larger rollout — I recommend approving the budget and a short procurement sync to lock the contract terms."

4) Suggested next steps for the calendar invite:
- 30-minute Procurement & InfoSec sync (Bianca + Elena + Aditya + Priyom)
- Pre-read: RIF-pilot-ROI-one-pager.pdf & Security-FAQ-answers.docx (sent)
- Goal: identify any absolute gating items and confirm pilot PO owner.

If this looks good I’ll hand these off to Aditya to send to Elena and Bianca. Tessa — if you can add one bullet on the DPA and deletion cadence (48–72 hours after test) to the security memo, we’ll be set.

—Priyom
